title: Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand Win Historic BWF World Championships Bronze, End India's 15-Year Wait
excerpt: The unseeded Indian duo staged a dramatic comeback against China's fourth seeds to reach the semifinals, securing India's first women's doubles medal at the BWF World Championships since 2011.
body:
• Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand won bronze in women's doubles at the 2026 BWF World Championships in New Delhi, ending India's 15-year medal drought in the event.
  • The unseeded Indian pair staged a dramatic comeback in the quarterfinals, beating fourth-seeded Chinese duo Jia Yifan and Zhang Shuxian 16-21, 21-15, 21-13 after trailing 0-6 in the opening game.
  • They lost the semifinal to top-seeded Chinese pair Liu Shengshu and Tan Ning, who won 18-21, 21-13, 21-8 after India took the first game.
  • The bronze extends India's streak of winning at least one medal at every BWF World Championships since 2011.

Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand have written a new chapter in Indian badminton history, winning the bronze medal in women's doubles at the 2026 BWF World Championships in New Delhi. It is India's first women's doubles medal at the tournament since Jwala Gutta and Ashwini Ponnappa claimed bronze in London in 2011.

The unseeded Indian pair, ranked 39th in the world, produced one of the most memorable runs of the tournament before falling to top-seeded Chinese pair Liu Shengshu and Tan Ning in the semifinals on Saturday.

The Quarterfinal That Changed Everything

The defining moment of their campaign came in Friday's quarterfinal against fourth-seeded Jia Yifan and Zhang Shuxian. The Chinese pair, who had beaten Treesa and Gayatri in all three of their previous meetings, raced to a 6-0 lead in the opening game and eventually took it 21-16.

What followed was a transformation. The Indian pair adjusted their tactics between games, shifting to a more aggressive approach with sharper net play and powerful cross-court smashes. They levelled the match by taking the second game 21-15, then dominated the decider, racing to an 11-5 lead at the interval before closing out 21-13.

"He always said just calm down and be in the present moment. I think that really worked today."

— Treesa Jolly, on coach Pullela Gopichand's advice

The 69-minute victory electrified the home crowd at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium and marked India's first women's doubles semifinal appearance at the World Championships in 15 years.

Semifinal Heartbreak Against Top Seeds

Treesa and Gayatri carried their momentum into Saturday's semifinal, taking the first game 21-18 against Liu and Tan. But the top-seeded Chinese pair responded decisively, winning the second game 21-13 and running away with the decider 21-8 to reach the final.

Liu and Tan went on to face third-seeded South Korean pair Baek Ha-na and Lee So-hee in the final, where the Koreans prevailed 21-15, 21-15 to claim the title.

A Comeback Built on Resilience

The bronze caps a remarkable year for the Indian partnership. Treesa suffered a severe ankle injury during training earlier in 2026, ahead of the Asian Championships and Uber Cup. After rehabilitation, the pair returned at the Indonesia Open, competed at the US Open, and won the Philippine International Challenge in early August — building form just weeks before the World Championships.

Gayatri, the daughter of legendary Indian badminton coach Pullela Gopichand, and Treesa, a 23-year-old from Kerala who became the first Malayali woman to medal at the BWF World Championships, have been partners since their formative years at the Pullela Gopichand Badminton Academy in Hyderabad.

Their coach B Sumeeth Reddy said preparations for the home World Championships had begun nearly two months in advance. "It started around 45-50 days before. Rather than just thinking about the World Championship, it was one day at a time," Reddy told reporters after the quarterfinal win, crediting Gopichand's planning.

India's Remarkable Medal Streak Continues

The bronze extends India's streak of winning at least one medal at every BWF World Championships since 2011. Indian shuttlers Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, the fifth-seeded men's doubles pair, had been aiming for a second Indian medal but lost in the quarterfinals to Chinese third seeds Liang Weikeng and Wang Chang.

The 2026 edition, hosted in India for the first time, saw dominant performances across events. France's Alex Lanier won men's singles gold, becoming the first Frenchman to claim the title, while South Korea's An Se-young retained the women's singles crown. French pair Thom Gicquel and Delphine Delrue also made history, winning the mixed doubles title — a first for France.

What's Next

Treesa and Gayatri's World Championships medal adds to a growing list of achievements that includes All England Open semifinal appearances in 2022 and 2023, a Commonwealth Games bronze in 2022, and back-to-back Syed Modi International titles. With the pair still in their early twenties, the bronze in New Delhi signals that India's best results in women's doubles may be ahead of them.
